document: Rule catalogue and fact cues for impact analysis (decision D-004, revised: evidence states are attributed per system and rule through evidence_subjects). Each rule's text is located live on every run, from the binding Article 50 paragraph in CONSOLIDATED (cross-checked against OJ and AMEND) or from the live POLICY page; if the text_cue is not found, the rule is unavailable and every row that depends on it is 'unresolved'. These are draft interpretation aids for Legal review, not legal conclusions.

rules.text_cue: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons
rules.summary: Providers design direct-interaction AI systems so people are informed they are interacting with AI, unless obvious; information given per Art. 50(5).
rules.new_action_text: Confirm with Legal whether the provider-side interaction-notice duty bears on this system

rules.text_cue: generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format
rules.summary: Providers of systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text mark outputs machine-readably and detectably.
rules.new_action_text: Confirm with Legal whether the provider-side marking duty bears on this system

rules.text_cue: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto
rules.summary: Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems inform exposed persons; information given per Art. 50(5).
rules.new_action_text: Supply current-release facts on emotion-recognition / biometric-categorisation use

rules.rule_ref: EU AI Act Art. 50(4) first subpara. (deep fake) [binding]
rules.text_cue: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose
rules.summary: Deployers disclose that deep-fake image, audio or video content is artificially generated or manipulated (limited for evidently artistic or fictional works); information given per Art. 50(5).
rules.new_action_text: Confirm deep-fake disclosure for published content

rules.rule_ref: EU AI Act Art. 50(4) second subpara. (public-interest text) [binding]
rules.text_cue: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest
rules.summary: Deployers disclose AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, unless human-reviewed under editorial responsibility.
rules.new_action_text: Confirm whether generated text is published to inform the public on matters of public interest

rules.rule_ref: AI-POL Learner and public transparency, bullet 1 (interaction notice) [internal policy]
rules.text_cue: must receive a clear notice before or at the first interaction
rules.summary: A person directly interacting with an AI system receives a clear notice before or at the first interaction unless the AI nature is obvious from context.
rules.new_action_text: Add and verify a first-interaction AI notice

rules.rule_ref: AI-POL Learner and public transparency, bullet 2 (machine-readable provenance) [internal policy]
rules.text_cue: must retain machine-readable provenance when the tool supports it
rules.summary: Public synthetic images, audio or video retain machine-readable provenance when the tool supports it.
rules.control_note: No structured source field verifies provenance; it needs a complete evidence record.
rules.new_action_text: Verify machine-readable provenance on published synthetic media

rules.rule_ref: AI-POL Learner and public transparency, bullet 2 (visible label unless Legal-approved exception) [internal policy]
rules.text_cue: also requires a visible label unless Legal approves a documented exception
rules.summary: The Communications owner requires a visible label on public synthetic media unless Legal approves a documented exception.
rules.new_action_text: Verify visible label or obtain a Legal decision on the exception

rules.rule_ref: AI-POL Learner and public transparency, bullet 3 (staff-only tool output route) [internal policy]
rules.text_cue: The owner must still record how generated material reaches learners or the public
rules.summary: Staff-only drafting tools are not automatically public interactions; the owner records how generated material reaches learners or the public.
rules.control_note: Needs a complete evidence record of the output route.
rules.new_action_text: Record how generated material reaches learners or the public

patterns: licenses and operates a third-party supplier's existing AI product
licensed_supplier_product.meaning: Systems listed in the same POLICY block are licensed supplier products; Quillhaven did not develop, commission or brand them.

patterns: does not classify biometric data or infer emotions
not used to identify or infer emotions or intentions or to assign people to categories from biometric data
no_emotion_or_biometric.meaning: POLICY states that the system does not perform emotion recognition or biometric categorisation.

patterns: has not yet established whether the flagging uses biometric data
emotion_or_biometric_unestablished.meaning: POLICY states that emotion-recognition or biometric use is not established.

patterns: not depictions of an existing person
not_existing_person_depiction.meaning: POLICY states that the generated media does not depict existing persons, places, objects or events as authentic.

patterns_all: could mistake it for an authentic recording
deep_fake_indicators.meaning: POLICY states that the content shows real people, could be mistaken for authentic, and is not evidently artistic or fictional.

patterns: not material published to inform the public about matters of public interest
not published or sent to applicants, learners or the general public
not_public_interest_text.meaning: POLICY states that the generated text is not published to inform the public on matters of public interest.

patterns: do not converse with the AI product
no_direct_conversation.meaning: POLICY states that the people concerned do not interact directly with the AI system.

interaction-notice.meaning: Records about AI-interaction notices or banners.

provenance-marking.meaning: Records about machine-readable marking or provenance metadata.

visible-label-disclosure.meaning: Records about visible labels, disclosure to viewers, or label exceptions (exception requests).

text-output-route.meaning: Records about how generated text reaches recipients or the public.

provider-role.meaning: Records about whether Quillhaven is the provider (applicability of provider-side duties).

emotion-biometric.meaning: Records about emotion recognition or biometric categorisation (applicability of Art. 50(3)).
